{{Quote|Within a decade the Trade Federation had upgraded spaceport facilities at Kirdo and Laria, established a depot for goods at Tyne Albamon, blazed a faster route to Svivren, and installed a TDF marine post at Dravian Station.|Memoirs of Firmus Kett|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
'''Laria''' was an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] celestial body located in the [[Rseik sector/Legends|Rseik sector]]. By [[3643 BBY]], dozens of [[Star map/Legends|star-charts]], accompanied by notes in a forgotten [[Language/Legends|language]], had been stored in [[Computer/Legends|computer]] banks inside ancient ruins on Laria. Around that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], [[Archaeologist/Legends|archaeologists]] were able to restore the [[Map/Legends|charts]]. [[Millennium/Legends|Millennia]] later, the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] improved the facilities of Laria's [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]].

==Description==
Laria was a terrestrial<ref name="Finding Our Way" /> celestial body<ref name="Author's Cut" /> located in the [[Laria system/Legends|Laria system]], a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Rseik sector/Legends|Rseik sector]].<ref name="EAOC" />

==History==
Long before<ref name="Finding Our Way" /> [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="Date">Per the reasoning [[Template:TOR_dates|here]], Act I of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'' takes place around [[3643 BBY]]. Since players of ''The Old Republic'' can assign their companions on the mission "Finding Our Way" independently of the main class storyline at any point during the [[Star Wars video games|game]], the mission must take place at some point around 3643 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]].</ref> dozens of [[Star map/Legends|star-charts]], accompanied by many notes, were stored in a series of [[Computer/Legends|computer]] banks in a structure on Laria. By 3643 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], the structure had been degraded to a series of ruins, and the [[Language/Legends|language]] in which the notes had been written had been forgotten.<ref name="Finding Our Way" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: The Old Republic}}
The [[Star/Legends|star]]-[[Map/Legends|charts]] in the Laria ruins were discovered around that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], with [[Archaeologist/Legends|archaeologists]] attempting to restore the documents. An individual affiliated with the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] eventually sent a companion to assist the researchers. The companion carefully restored the charts, which were subsequently turned over to the highly grateful [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi Council]]<ref name="Finding Our Way" /> of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="SWTORE">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref>
{{Endgame}}

Within a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] of extending its operations to the Rseik [[Sector/Legends|sector]] following the [[Bordal Contagion]] of [[214 BBY]], the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] upgraded the facilities of Laria's [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]]. The astronomical object was eventually mentioned in the memoirs of the [[Trade Defense Force]] [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Firmus Kett]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:The_Old_Republic_cover.png|thumb|right|250px|Laria was first mentioned in ''Star Wars: The Old Republic''.]]
Laria was mentioned in a Slicing Crew Skill mission of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[2011]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] developed by [[BioWare]]. The mission was originally only available to Galactic Republic&ndash;aligned player characters, though both that restriction and the information regarding the mission's outcome was later removed from the game.<ref name="Finding Our Way" /> The [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Laria [[Star system/Legends|system]], and therefore the celestial body Laria, in grid square N-19.<ref name="EAOC" />

Laria was originally meant to be mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the sidebar that would have mentioned the celestial body was cut before the book's release. The information regarding Laria was later released in [[2014]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the StarWars.com [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Author's Cut" />
